questions.question: A seller sold two cycles for Rs. 6000 each but on one he gained 20% and on the other he lost 20% then what will be the total gain or loss percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A seller sold two cycles for Rs. 6000 each but on one he gained 20% and on the other he lost 20% then what will be the total gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When Selling Price (SP) is same for two articles, and one is sold at x% profit and another at x% loss, there is always a net loss.

Net Loss % = (x ÷ 10)2 %

Given x = 20%

Net Loss % = (20 ÷ 10)2 = 22 = 4%

∴ The correct answer is 4% loss.

Alternate Method

Given: SP of cycle 1 = ₹6000, SP of cycle 2 = ₹6000, Gain% = 20%, Loss% = 20%

Formula Used: Cost Price (CP) = SP × [100 ÷ (100 ± P/L %)]

⇒ CP of first cycle = 6000 × (100 ÷ 120) = ₹5000

⇒ CP of second cycle = 6000 × (100 ÷ 80) = ₹7500

⇒ Total CP = 5000 + 7500 = ₹12500

⇒ Total SP = 6000 + 6000 = ₹12000

⇒ Total Loss = 12500 − 12000 = ₹500

⇒ Loss % = (500 ÷ 12500) × 100 = 4%

∴ The correct answer is 4% loss.

Additional Information

Same Cost Price Case

If two articles are bought at the same CP and one is sold at x% profit and another at x% loss, the net result is always No Profit No Loss.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the effective net change is [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100] %.

Dishonest Dealer Formula

Profit % = [ (Error) ÷ (True Value − Error) ] × 100, where error is the weight difference.

questions.question: A retailer sells an article at Rs. 150 less than the marked price and gains a profit of 25%. Find the marked price of the article (in Rs.), if its cost price is Rs. 2500.
questions.questionHtml: A retailer sells an article at Rs. 150 less than the marked price and gains a profit of 25%. Find the marked price of the article (in Rs.), if its cost price is Rs. 2500.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit = 25% ⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 125% of Cost Price (CP)

SP = 1.25 × 2500 = ₹3125

Marked Price (MP) = SP + Discount

MP = 3125 + 150 = ₹3275

∴ The correct answer is ₹3275.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) = ₹2500

Profit Percentage = 25%

Discount = ₹150

Formula Used:

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit

Marked Price (MP) = SP + Discount

Calculations:

⇒ Profit = (25/100) × 2500 = ₹625

⇒ SP = ₹2500 + ₹625 = ₹3125

⇒ MP = ₹3125 + ₹150 = ₹3275

∴ The correct answer is ₹3275.

Additional Information

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price can be directly calculated using the formula: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Markup Percentage

Markup % is the percentage by which the Cost Price is increased to reach the Marked Price: Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Discount % = (Discount / MP) × 100.

questions.question: Two friends X and Y purchased a generator for Rs. 2,00,000. They sold it after 5 months wherein X received a profit of Rs. 25,000. X and Y made profit in a ratio of 2 : 3 in the generator. Calculate the selling price of a generator.
questions.questionHtml: Two friends X and Y purchased a generator for Rs. 2,00,000. They sold it after 5 months wherein X received a profit of Rs. 25,000. X and Y made profit in a ratio of 2 : 3 in the generator. Calculate the selling price of a generator.
questions.solution:
Formula used:

Selling price = Cost price + Profit

Calculations:

Ratio of total profit earned = X : Y = 2 : 3

Let, total profit be Rs. A

Profit earned by X = (2/5) × A

⇒ 25,000 = (2/5) × A

⇒ 25,000 × 5/2 = A

⇒ A = Rs. 62,500

⇒ S.P. = Rs. 2,00,000 + Rs. 62,500

∴ Selling price of generator is Rs. 2,62,500

questions.question: Anikitha sold her text book for a loss of 15%. If she would have sold the textbook for an increased price of Rs. 150, there would have been gain of 10%. What was the cost price of the text book? (Used)
questions.questionHtml: Anikitha sold her text book for a loss of 15%. If she would have sold the textbook for an increased price of Rs. 150, there would have been gain of 10%. What was the cost price of the text book? (Used)
questions.solution:
Cost price × ((110/100) – (85/100)) = 150

⇒ Cost price × (25/100) = 150

After cross multiplying ⇒ Cost price = Rs. 600

questions.question: Amar and Samar sold their horses at Rs 2,420 each, but Amar incurred a loss of 20%, while Samar gained 10%. What is the ratio of the cost price of the horses of Samar to that of Amar?
questions.questionHtml: Amar and Samar sold their horses at Rs 2,420 each, but Amar incurred a loss of 20%, while Samar gained 10%. What is the ratio of the cost price of the horses of Samar to that of Amar?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Cost Price (CP) = 1/(100 ± Profit/Loss%) when Selling Price (SP) is constant.

Amar (Loss 20%) → CPA factor = 1/80

Samar (Gain 10%) → CPS factor = 1/110

Ratio of CPS : CPA = (1/110) : (1/80) = 80 : 110 = 8 : 11.

∴ The correct answer is 8 : 11.

Alternate Method

Given:

Selling Price (SP) of each horse = Rs 2,420

Amar's loss = 20%

Samar's gain = 10%

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 / (100 ± Profit/Loss%)

Calculations:

⇒ Amar's horse CP = 2420 × 100 / (100 − 20)

⇒ CPAmar = 2420 × 100 / 80 = 2420 × 5 / 4 = 605 × 5 = Rs 3,025

⇒ Samar's horse CP = 2420 × 100 / (100 + 10)

⇒ CPSamar = 2420 × 100 / 110 = 2420 / 1.1 = Rs 2,200

⇒ Ratio of CP of Samar to CP of Amar = 2200 : 3025

⇒ Dividing both by 25: 88 : 121

⇒ Dividing both by 11: 8 : 11

∴ The correct answer is 8 : 11.

Additional Information

Common Selling Price Case

If two articles are sold at the same price, one at a profit of x% and another at a loss of x%, there is always a net loss of (x/10)2%.

Cost Price Calculation

The formula CP = SP × 100 / (100 + P%) or CP = SP × 100 / (100 − L%) is the fundamental method to find the initial value.

Ratio Conversion

To simplify a ratio like (1/a) : (1/b), simply cross-multiply to get b : a, which is useful when the numerator (SP) is common.

questions.question: P sold a pillow to Q at 20% profit and Q sold to S at 15% loss. If P sold it to S at the selling price of Q, then what is the profit% or loss% P would make?
questions.questionHtml: P sold a pillow to Q at 20% profit and Q sold to S at 15% loss. If P sold it to S at the selling price of Q, then what is the profit% or loss% P would make?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Cost Price (CP) of P = 100 units.

P sells to Q at 20% profit → Q's CP = 120 units.

Q sells to S at 15% loss → Q's SP = 120 − (15% of 120) = 120 − 18 = 102 units.

If P sells to S at Q's selling price (102 units), P's profit = 102 − 100 = 2 units.

Profit% = (2 ÷ 100) × 100 = 2%.

∴ The correct answer is 2% profit.

Alternate Method

Given:

Profit of P = 20% | Loss of Q = 15%

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 or CP × (100 − Loss%)/100

Step-by-step Calculations:

⇒ Let the Cost Price for P (CPP) = 100.

⇒ Selling Price for P (SPP) = 100 × (120 ÷ 100) = 120.

⇒ This SP for P is the Cost Price for Q (CPQ) = 120.

⇒ Selling Price for Q (SPQ) = 120 × (100 − 15) ÷ 100 = 120 × 0.85 = 102.

⇒ If P sells to S at the SP of Q, then new SP for P (SPP_new) = 102.

⇒ Profit for P = SPP_new − CPP = 102 − 100 = 2.

⇒ Profit% for P = (Profit ÷ CPP) × 100 = (2 ÷ 100) × 100 = 2%.

∴ The correct answer is 2% profit.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by x% and then y%, the net change is given by [x + y + (xy ÷ 100)]%. For loss, use a negative sign.

Profit and Loss Relationship

Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. If the result is negative, it indicates a Loss%.

Effective Cost Price

In a chain of transactions, the Selling Price of one person becomes the Cost Price for the next person in the sequence.

questions.question: Selling price of 9 articles is equal to the cost price of 15 articles. Find the gain or loss percent in the transaction.
questions.questionHtml: Selling price of 9 articles is equal to the cost price of 15 articles. Find the gain or loss percent in the transaction.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Selling Price (SP) to Cost Price (CP) is obtained by inverting the given values.

9 × SP = 15 × CP ⇒ SP / CP = 15 / 9 = 5 / 3.

Profit = SP − CP = 5 − 3 = 2 units.

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (2 / 3) × 100 = 66 2/3%.

∴ The correct answer is 66 2/3% profit.

Alternate Method

Given: Selling price of 9 articles = Cost price of 15 articles.

Let the cost price of 1 article be ₹1.

⇒ Cost price of 15 articles = ₹15.

⇒ Selling price of 9 articles = ₹15 (as given in the question).

⇒ Cost price of 9 articles = ₹9.

⇒ Profit on 9 articles = SP − CP = ₹15 − ₹9 = ₹6.

⇒ Profit percentage = (Profit / CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (6 / 9) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (2 / 3) × 100 = 200/3%

⇒ Profit % = 66 2/3%.

∴ The correct answer is 66 2/3% profit.

Additional Information

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100 and Loss % = [(CP − SP) / CP] × 100. Both are always calculated on the Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

Direct Relation for x SP = y CP

If the SP of x articles equals the CP of y articles, then Profit/Loss % = [(y − x) / x] × 100. A positive result indicates profit, and a negative result indicates loss.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount. The relation between CP and MP is given by CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

questions.question: By selling an article for Rs. 1,170, Elisa suffers as much loss as she would have gained by selling it at a profit of 22%. If she sells it for Rs. 1,450, then her profit/loss per cent (correct up to one decimal place) is:
questions.questionHtml: By selling an article for Rs. 1,170, Elisa suffers as much loss as she would have gained by selling it at a profit of 22%. If she sells it for Rs. 1,450, then her profit/loss per cent (correct up to one decimal place) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Cost Price (CP) be 100%.

As Loss equals profit of 22%, the first Selling Price (SP) = 100% − 22% = 78%.

⇒ 78% = ₹1,170 ⇒ 100% = (1,170 ÷ 78) × 100 = ₹1,500.

New SP = ₹1,450 ⇒ Loss = 1,500 − 1,450 = ₹50.

Loss% = (50 ÷ 1500) × 100 = 3.33... ≈ 3.3%.

∴ The correct answer is Loss, 3.3.

Alternate Method

Given:

SP1 = ₹1,170

Profit% (for comparison) = 22%

SP2 = ₹1,450

Formula Used:

Loss = CP − SP | Profit = SP − CP | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

Calculations:

Let the Cost Price of the article be x.

According to the question, Loss at ₹1,170 = Profit at 22%.

⇒ x − 1,170 = 22% of x

⇒ x − 1,170 = 0.22x

⇒ x − 0.22x = 1,170

⇒ 0.78x = 1,170

⇒ x = 1,170 ÷ 0.78 = 1,500

The Cost Price (CP) is ₹1,500.

Now, if the article is sold for ₹1,450 (SP2):

⇒ Loss = CP − SP2 = 1,500 − 1,450 = ₹50

⇒ Loss% = (50 ÷ 1,500) × 100

⇒ Loss% = 10 ÷ 3 = 3.33...

Rounding to one decimal place, we get 3.3%.

∴ The correct answer is Loss, 3.3.

Additional Information

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

Selling Price Calculation

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 or SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100. Use these to find SP directly from CP and percentage change.

Cost Price as Base

Assuming CP = 100 units simplifies calculations. A 22% profit makes SP = 122 units, while a 22% loss makes SP = 78 units.

questions.question: A fruit seller buys some oranges at the rate of 4 for ₹ 10 and an equal number more at 5 for ₹ 10. Then he sells the whole lot at the rate of 9 for ₹ 20. What is his loss or gain percentage ?
questions.questionHtml: A fruit seller buys some oranges at the rate of 4 for ₹ 10 and an equal number more at 5 for ₹ 10. Then he sells the whole lot at the rate of 9 for ₹ 20. What is his loss or gain percentage ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the number of oranges bought of each type be the LCM of 4, 5, and 9, which is 180.

Total CP of (180 + 180) oranges = (10 ÷ 4) × 180 + (10 ÷ 5) × 180 = 450 + 360 = ₹810.

Total SP of 360 oranges = (20 ÷ 9) × 360 = ₹800.

Loss = 810 − 800 = ₹10.

Loss % = (10 ÷ 810) × 100 = 100/81% = 119/81%.

∴ The correct answer is Loss percent 119/81%.

Alternate Method

Given:

CP of 1st type = ₹10 for 4 oranges

CP of 2nd type = ₹10 for 5 oranges

SP of mixed lot = ₹20 for 9 oranges

Formula Used:

Loss = CP − SP

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

Calculation:

⇒ CP of 1 orange of 1st type = 10 ÷ 4 = ₹2.5

⇒ CP of 1 orange of 2nd type = 10 ÷ 5 = ₹2

⇒ Since equal quantities are mixed, Average CP per orange = (2.5 + 2) ÷ 2 = ₹2.25 = ₹9/4

⇒ SP of 1 orange from the combined lot = 20 ÷ 9 = ₹20/9

⇒ Since Average CP > SP, there is a Loss.

⇒ Loss per orange = 9/4 − 20/9 = (81 − 80) ÷ 36 = ₹1/36

⇒ Loss % = (Loss ÷ Average CP) × 100 = (1/36 ÷ 9/4) × 100

⇒ Loss % = (1/36 × 4/9) × 100 = 100/81% = 119/81%

∴ The correct answer is Loss percent 119/81%.

Additional Information

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: Selling Price = MP × (1 − Discount% ÷ 100).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the effective single discount is calculated as: Effective Discount = (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price but uses a false weight, his gain percentage is given by: Gain % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

questions.question: Annie bought two phones Foni and Vokia for a total of Rs. 83000. She then sold Foni at a profit of 20% and Vokia at a loss of 10%. The ratio of the selling price of Foni and Vokia is 13 : 11. Find the cost price of Vokia.
questions.questionHtml: Annie bought two phones Foni and Vokia for a total of Rs. 83000. She then sold Foni at a profit of 20% and Vokia at a loss of 10%. The ratio of the selling price of Foni and Vokia is 13 : 11. Find the cost price of Vokia.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Cost Price (CP) = (SP Ratio) ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss%)

Foni : Vokia CP Ratio = (13 / 120) : (11 / 90)

CP Ratio = (13 × 3) : (11 × 4) = 39 : 44

Total Ratio = 39 + 44 = 83 units → ₹83,000

Vokia CP = 44 units = ₹44,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹44000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total cost price of Foni and Vokia = ₹83,000

Profit on Foni = 20% | Loss on Vokia = 10%

Ratio of Selling Price (SPF : SPV) = 13 : 11

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%) / 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the cost price of Foni be CF and Vokia be CV.

⇒ SPF = CF × 120/100 = 1.2CF

⇒ SPV = CV × 90/100 = 0.9CV

⇒ (1.2CF) / (0.9CV) = 13 / 11

⇒ (12CF / 9CV) = 13 / 11

⇒ (4CF / 3CV) = 13 / 11

⇒ CF / CV = (13 × 3) / (11 × 4) = 39 / 44

⇒ Total CP units = 39 + 44 = 83 units

⇒ 83 units = 83000 ⇒ 1 unit = 1000

⇒ Cost Price of Vokia = 44 × 1000 = 44000

∴ The correct answer is ₹44000.

Additional Information

Cost Price and Selling Price Relation

Profit is always calculated on the CP unless stated otherwise. SP = CP + Profit or SP = CP − Loss.

Ratio of CP when SPs are given

If SP is constant, the ratio of CP of two articles is inversely proportional to their (100 ± P/L)% multipliers.

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Selling Price can also be calculated from Marked Price as SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100.
